finding.claim: Mail::Message.from_yaml loads untrusted YAML through Psych safe_load, but the permitted classes include the delivery-method classes (Mail::Sendmail, Mail::Exim, Mail::FileDelivery, Mail::SMTP, and others). from_yaml then copies any '@'-prefixed key into an instance variable with no allowlist. A crafted document can set @delivery_method to an attacker-chosen delivery object with attacker-chosen settings. Message#deliver then runs it: Sendmail executes an attacker-chosen binary with attacker-chosen arguments, and FileDelivery appends message content to an attacker-chosen path.
finding.source: YAML string passed to Mail::Message.from_yaml(str) (lib/mail/message.rb:1850-1851). Precondition: the application deserializes YAML it does not fully control (stored or queued messages, cross-tenant data) and then calls deliver or deliver!.
finding.sink: Sendmail#deliver! builds argv from settings[:location] and settings[:arguments] and calls IO.popen (lib/mail/network/delivery_methods/sendmail.rb:63-80). FileDelivery#deliver! opens settings[:location]/basename(to+settings[:extension]) in append mode (lib/mail/network/delivery_methods/file_delivery.rb:33-39). Both are reached through Message#deliver -> do_delivery (lib/mail/message.rb:250-259, 2145-2148).

trace.note: permitted_classes list; lines 11-20 include the delivery-method classes and Mail.delivery_method.class
safe_load restricts which classes can be instantiated, not the ivar values those permitted objects receive (Psych sets ivars directly, so attacker-chosen settings reach the object)
'@' keys passed to instance_variable_set with no allowlist, so '@delivery_method' can hold the attacker's Sendmail or FileDelivery object
delivery_method reader returns @delivery_method when no argument is given (line 276)
deliver calls do_delivery when no delivery_handler is set (lines 252-255)
do_delivery calls delivery_method.deliver!(self) when perform_deliveries is true (line 2148)
IO.popen(command, ...) with an array argv, so no shell, but the executable and its arguments are attacker-chosen
path from settings[:location] and settings[:extension]; basename applies only to the recipient
File.open(path, 'a') with attacker-chosen directory: arbitrary file append

finding.guards_checked: Psych safe_load class allowlist (yaml.rb:23-27): enforced for class instantiation only. No allowlist on instance-variable names or on values of permitted delivery classes. Sendmail uses an argv array with '--' before recipients, so there is no shell injection on the envelope fields (sendmail.rb:63-70). Delivery is not automatic: it requires the app to call deliver or deliver!. Not verified: the exact Psych version behavior in the target environment, and whether the app calls from_yaml on untrusted input.
